recommendation.summary: Stay on the languages the team already knows and move each one to its current long-term-support release: Java 21 with Spring Boot 3 for the rules, web API and batch; rebuild only the portal, in React and TypeScript, because AngularJS has no upgrade path; Python 3.12 for the reports. Run it all as containers on Azure Container Apps with managed MySQL 8.0, delivered from the Azure DevOps pipelines already in use.
rationale: Same-language upgrades for four of five components keep risk and cost down — upgrade tooling (OpenRewrite) covers most of the Java 7/8 → 21 move.
Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.3 are long-term-support releases, supported well past the 2027 deadline.
AngularJS reached end of life in 2021 with no upgrade path; React with TypeScript is the most hireable replacement.
Azure Container Apps fits the stateless web API and scheduled jobs without running Kubernetes, and keeps data in US Azure regions.
Managed MySQL 8.0 removes the unsupported MySQL 5.6 with the fewest application changes.

alternatives.why_not: Discards working, tested Java rules and the team's Java skills; far above the $450k budget.

alternatives.option: Lift and shift the VMs to Azure as they are
alternatives.why_not: Keeps Java 7, Python 2.7 and AngularJS — fixes the lease but none of the audit findings.
More to operate than a five-component system needs; Container Apps covers it.
